newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle seen steady to lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent a lb lower and feeder cattle steady to 0.100 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Carryover pressure from the posting of lowest price levels since June 28 was expected in live cattle futures after cash beef prices and fed cattle prices slipped further Monday. Beef values declined to lowest levels since September 27 and feedlots sold cattle Monday at $70 per cwt, down $1 from last week's tops and down $3 from two weeks ago, analysts said.
However, the market is looking oversold and could rebound at any time, some market watchers said.
Expectations for a USDA Cattle-on-Feed report slated for Friday release may also influence the market, they added.

Early estimates on the report ranged from 93.8 to 97 percent of a year ago for on-feed cattle supplies at major feedlots. Placements were seen ranging from 96.2 to 102 percent and compare with large placements last year while marketing estimates were seen ranging from 85 to 90.8 percent.

Feeder cattle futures were seen showing weaker on a lower CME Feeder Cattle index, weaker cash feeder markets and early indications for higher corn futures, analysts said. Action in live cattle will also influence the market, they added.
The latest CME feeder index was off $0.06 at $62.98 per cwt.
